strengths: Excellent company research - demonstrates genuine understanding of Marker Learning's mission and a16z backing
Specific, verifiable metrics throughout resume (tens of thousands of documents, Fortune-200, 300+ users)
Honest acknowledgment of skill gap between Python backend experience and React/Node.js requirements
Strong opening hook in cover letter with concrete project example, not generic company flattery
Document intelligence and RAG experience in regulated biopharma is genuinely unique and relevant to healthcare AI
Clean, scannable resume formatting with good use of white space
weaknesses: Major skill gap: Role requires React and Node.js but resume shows only Python backend experience (TypeScript listed in skills but not demonstrated in any experience bullet)
Experience gap: Role lists 8-10+ years; candidate has ~4.5 years (2021-present), acknowledged as 'a significant stretch'
ATS risk: Core keywords (React, Node.js) missing from experience section - may not pass initial filters
Cover letter has slightly formulaic AI-generated feel in middle paragraphs ('The precision required...mirrors what I developed' structure)
No demonstrated full-stack experience - this is a Lead Full-Stack role requiring both frontend and backend leadership
Some outcome metrics missing: what was the business impact of the RAG pipeline? Time saved? Accuracy improved?
revision_suggestions: If you have ANY React/Node.js experience (personal projects, bootcamp, minor work tasks), add it to experience section - even a single bullet demonstrating frontend work would help ATS and credibility
Consider applying for a backend-focused or AI/ML engineer role at Marker Learning instead - your RAG and document intelligence experience is strong but mismatched to Lead Full-Stack
Tighten cover letter middle section - the second and third paragraphs feel slightly templated. Replace 'The precision required...mirrors what I developed' with a more specific connection
Add outcome metrics to resume bullets: What accuracy did the reranker achieve? How much faster was document retrieval? What submission success rate resulted?
If committed to this application, add a brief technical project to resume showing React/TypeScript work - demonstrate you're actively building in the target stack
